PL8 -- Rationalizing the complex scalar, including zero periods

EL3 -- Elementary row-degree bound by a generic block column operation
Status: derived_alternative_proof
statement: For f in the column-invariant degree-nu module, every monomial has total degree at most sum_{i<=r}nu_i in the first r rows. Localize the generic matrix at the determinant of its top-left r-by-r block and kill the top-right block by earlier-column additions. The required upper-unipotent coefficients are independent of the row-scaling indeterminate, so the degree bound descends by injectivity of localization.

EL9 -- The normalized neighbor sum sends ball sections to dual sections
Status: faithful_translation
statement: The actual operator is (Y_v F)(L)=p^A_v sum_{L'->L_v}F(L[v:=L']). Incoming edges form a finite set. Normalized edge integrality gives the tensor-valued slot inclusion termwise. EL10 -- Normalized error transport used in the joint-rank cancellation
Status: derived_simplification
statement: For an edge e and c>=0, p^A(w^c R_e) subset w^c P_t(e.tgt). Thus a test vector vanishing to order w^c at an unwanted edge produces a normalized contribution in the corresponding w^c dual slot. When c>=2(D+1) this lies in p^(D+1)P_t; the source retains its stronger global cStar>=4(D+1) assumption.

IP7 -- Literal split-product identity and direct weighted normal homogeneity
Status: derived_simplification
statement: For each actual PGen, prod_plTan gives P as the product of its joined split columns. A column's block changes once per used letter; the normal weighted degree is exactly the sum of p^(z-s_i) at costly steps. The source size bound N+r<=K keeps every negative column above the rank boundary. Parity is preserved by reduction modulo even n'.

Status: faithful_translation

Status: faithful_translation

Status: derived_simplification

CL1 -- An explicit complementary standard-monomial family
Status: faithful_translation
statement: At a selected even twist use arrays e with e(0,0)=nu_0; at a selected odd twist use arrays with zero first row. Deleting respectively the first row/column or first row/last column identifies these with tail-shape arrays. Odd reversal gives lambda^0_2 minus the reversed original tail. Thus n2 is the product of D_(k-1)(tail) on selected twists and D_k(lambda^0) elsewhere.
assumptions: ["Dominant integral weights and the selected-flat/remainder decomposition of WeightHyp."]

PG3 -- Weighted Fock lattices, algebraic orders and actual cutoff projectors
Status: faithful_translation
statement: The lattice b(F)>=0 is full, torus-graded and divided-power stable for arbitrary ramification, by the half-sum of two binomial valuations. Apply the companion IW4 to the S-letter weight interval [-D_S,D_S], using the difference of the same coordinate in two weights <=2D_S. The cutoff ord_S>=theta is the sum of isotypic components with last highest weight>=ceil(theta). Its Fock projector is selfadjoint; nested/disjoint cutoff projectors commute. PG5 -- Marked path columns give the actual model lift
Status: faithful_translation
statement: Expand in the integral prefix-adapted signed path-column basis. Mark columns containing a base letter; only in those columns move frame indices m>0 to tangent variables. Tangent degree is bounded by the number of marked columns<=dLL. Unmarked columns have nonpositive colVal and no variables in the renamed link, so the original prefix order lower bounds survive. Injective renaming preserves each column Gauss valuation and its multiplicativity proves integrality of the full renamed product. Digit-split the remaining labels to obtain integral good Z with phi Z=H and no further link loss.

PG6 -- The joint chain projector has controlled coefficients and preserves every label/tangent block
Status: faithful_translation
statement: Form the product of the weakened chain cutoff projectors. Its sets are nested within segments, disjoint across segments, and contained in or disjoint from every relevant link set. It therefore preserves links. Euler commutation fixes every outside label/tangent exponent. On good x^zeta it has b>=v_p(zeta!)/2-Dm; within the resulting block factorial valuations differ by at most kp, so all coefficients are >=-Dm-kp/2. Hence p^ceil(Dm+kp/2) clears its coefficients on integral good inputs.
assumptions: ["The cutoff projector construction and bounds in PG3.", "The good-exponent conditions and actual chain/link letter sets of PG1."]
depends_on: ["PG1", "PG3"]
proof_location: {"file": "local_gram_section.tex", "anchors": ["PG6"]}

CG1 -- Actual paired-path basis, saturation, and reduction of XX′
Status: derived_simplification
statement: For any domain R, the source XX′ is the span of exactly the integral paired Psi basis indexed by segPairs. The normal-order projector keeps or kills each whole paired multidegree block. Therefore XX′ over O is saturated, its reduction is XX′ over the residue field, and total-letter-degree projection preserves it. This proves the first, third and sixth NestedTypeBound clauses used in the lift and RestLam.
assumptions: ["The previously reconstructed universal integral signed-path basis and exact simultaneous prefix filtration adaptation, IP3–IP4.", "The source hypotheses valid frame, segN+r<=K and nonnegative integer margins are retained in application. The basis argument itself works without the latter two restrictions."]
depends_on: ["IP3", "IP4"]

CG4 -- Internal coarse degrees and the oldest-letter dichotomy
Status: faithful_translation
statement: A nonzero actual coarse generator has degree a′. An intermediate physical row occurs in only one segment, so a′=p^(dist+R)*b+label degree and the label bound yields b>a′/p^(dist+R)−k. GP9 -- Antidiagonal specialization and integral independence
Status: complete_human_proof_using_IP_integral_path_basis
statement: Killing off-antidiagonal terminal plane variables turns each actual plane path word into a unit times a frame monomial times its truncated-path word. Icut is standard and records every terminal column rise. The IP product basis gives specialized independence; taking the least auxiliary off-diagonal degree lifts it, and cancelling the nonzero common determinant-monomial gives RestInd.

JR5 -- Neighbor evaluation isolates any good coordinate
Status: faithful_translation

OR3 -- Overlapping tasks and the literal segment divisor
Status: faithful_translation
statement: A finite list of determinant tasks of total exponent T can be extracted if every initial task prefix has minimum at least its other-vector degree plus T. Each quotient has weakly smaller degrees and every prefix loses at most T. For actual segments the tasks are one recent-r-even determinant per late letter plus the preceding-frame determinant; their total cost is <=mStar, and their quotient satisfies exactly MGen0.

OR7 -- The literal RestPh congruence and residual exponent arithmetic
Status: faithful_translation
statement: Universal Frobenius determinant congruence modulo p and the binomial split give phi(Dseg_x)^m1 divisible modulo p^c by D_barx^(m1−c), and similarly the old-frame factor. Late intervals cover each TT residue once; cyclic frame reindexing and m1−c=(2Q+3)c+kQ, m2−c=c(alphaMax+1) yield product phi(Dv)=fixedSymbolFactor(c) DkQ H+p^cY with H integral tangential and Y integral.

GG6 -- Orthogonal graded projection with cost (K+1)e1 and exact zero-prefix handling
Status: derived_simplification
statement: For K>=1 there is a rational Fock-orthogonal projection onto V_e, integral after p^((K+1)e1). The K+2 type projections commute; prefix0 and prefix1 are identity or zero, leaving K paid projections and one highest projection. For K=0 the actual nonzero graded lattice is a monomial line with Gram entry 1/binom(d,e).
assumptions: ["p is prime, coefficients are Q_p with coefficient lattice Z_p, and v_p(p)=1.", "The signed word has K+1 letters, r>=2 coordinates, rho=r-1, and its final letter is a vector.", "Each letter has a fixed nonnegative integral degree; there are finitely many prefix constraints with thresholds in Z union {infinity}.", "Standard characteristic-zero split-GL highest-weight theory and elementary DVR/Smith theory are declared background. Integral denominator statements use the already proved IW1-IW4."]

RU1 -- Actual SSZ block rank and its factorial-weighted lattice
Status: derived_simplification
statement: The actual block rank equals the sum over legal levels of dim(Y_level) h_r(B-j_plus). The factorial-weighted block lattice has exactly the same rational span and rank.

NP2 supplies this record uniformly; the numerical threshold theorem is not reproved here.", "The exact integral path basis and prefix adaptation are prior proved IP3-IP4; CB3 supplies the exact tableau dimension, and SW1/SW10 supply the named actual block and degree interfaces.", "Elementary field extension, polynomial coefficient algebra, finite-dimensional linear algebra and DVR/Smith normal form are declared classical background."]

BC2 -- Finite complete-DVR normalization and an embedding inducing the selected finite place
Status: derived_simplification
statement: A finite extension of the fraction field of a complete characteristic-zero DVR has finite free complete-DVR integral closure. For each number-field prime over p, some embedding tau into an algebraic closure of K_s induces exactly that prime; E_tau=K_s tau(L), S_tau and embRec satisfy tau(x) integral iff v(x)>=0.

The pointwise StdSubAt conclusion applies to recC data or supplied RingCompatibleAt identifications. BC3 -- Faithful descent and exact finite-free lattice, dual, intersection and valuation transport
Status: derived_simplification
statement: For a finite compatible inclusion R->S of DVRs, S has an R-basis beginning with 1. All R-defined submodules in a K-space extend coordinatewise, so arbitrary intersections, kernels and lattice duals commute, inclusions descend, and saturation/ranks are preserved. Integer valuations and module lengths scale by the ramification index; p-normalized valuations and lengths do not change.
assumptions: ["All coefficient rings in the application are DVR domains with compatible fraction-field embeddings. The source unramified ring W, its field Q, Frobenius and lattice edges stay fixed.", "BC1 uses the literal p>=5, f>=2 and Even f. Its field/Witt-vector existence and Teichmuller expansions are declared classical background; the required finite, quadratic, square-root and residue properties are proved in the report.", "BC2 proves the complete-DVR integral-closure and chosen-place construction, using only standard characteristic-zero separability, trace linear algebra and number-field integer-ring facts.", "CB1-CB2 and CB7 are prior proved integral tableau-basis/change-of-basis results; no integral semisimplicity premise is introduced.", "The full globally compatible family is not constructed here. The pointwise StdSubAt conclusion applies to recC data or supplied RingCompatibleAt identifications. Eventual compatible ring data can come from IsRecCEv or directly from GroupCompatibilityFamily; neither route is required simultaneously with the other.", "The formulas using normalized p-valuations concern the mixed-characteristic setting with p nonzero and nonunit; zero is treated by the usual value +infinity."]
depends_on: ["BC2"]

BO2 -- Biased marked cells and the unchanged marked-tile constant

CI16 -- Actual local constants and reference local-value arithmetic
Status: derived_simplification
statement: Primitive q^D roots and local integer representatives construct the exact Weil additive character. The canonical type Gauss sum squares to q for q=1 mod4. Twist twSqrt requires only square=q. Tame approximation plus the Hecke product formula supplies local reference values in K. These give the nine actual LocCst.Ok fields and initial/canonical constants.
assumptions: ["E is a number field; the actual prime P, residue map, coefficient field K of characteristic zero, and local coordinates are fixed. Except for CI3, every local calculation requiring digit representatives uses the literal DegOneUnram condition: q=Norm(P) is prime and q is not in P squared. The finite row/twist-prime family, ranks, character ties and constants have their explicitly stated hypotheses.", "No Lean compilation, kernel replay, formalization of the shorter human proofs, source modification, PDF build, prime-window existence, arbitrary Pins.iX, Later existence or proof of RH/GRH is asserted.", "Actual Hecke characters, integral infinity weights, coefficient-field containment, unit xi0, residue character ties and supplied twist q^D roots/square roots are explicit arithmetic inputs. The finite reference value field comes from TL14."]
depends_on: ["CI1", "TL14", "TL15"]

LS9 -- Frobenius injectivity through divided-power completion
Status: derived_simplification
statement: Witt Frobenius is injective on the completed divided-power ring and on its t-localization. The finite coefficient induction with explicit indices proves the required divisibility on A[w/p]; bounded truncations then prove completion injectivity.
assumptions: ["The local prime is any rational prime, including two; Omega is the algebraic closure of Q_p and C its completion with |p|=p^-1. Ordinary finite-extension valuation theory, profinite Galois theory, finite fields, Witt identities and the defining completion/localization constructions are background. The actual Fontaine rings are constructed and identified, not replaced by an abstract field model.", "Human mathematical reconstruction only: no Lean compilation/kernel replay, no formalization of replacement arguments and no RH/GRH claim. Stage existence uses the exact supplied Base, Cols and adapted RowsRest; it does not construct a nonempty arithmetic twist-reading family or comparison functors for geometric representations."]
depends_on: ["LS4", "LS6", "LS7", "LS8"]

Status: derived_simplification
statement: For every rational prime p there exist a LocPrime P, LocAinf AI and LocTied P AI on the specified Fontaine rings, including all finite-K equalities, normalized valuations, integral filtration and logarithmic clauses. Choosing them for all primes gives LocStage.
